text:
A: Hiya! Oh, I recognise your kitchen, the drawings on the fridge! I'm Hannah, in Norwich.
B: Hi. Hardik, Kingsbury. Yeah, she does a lot of drawings.
A: My daughter's exactly the same. Isla's nine, and it's horses, just horses, every single day. What does yours draw?
B: Anaya, she's six. Mostly cats at the moment. And hamsters, cos she wants one.
A: Oh no, she's campaigning!
B: Yeah, every day. I'm trying to hold out.
A: Good luck with that. So what do you do, Hardik?
B: Supermarket, replenishment. Stacking shelves, deliveries. Part-time, half nine to half two, so I can do the school runs.
A: Oh, that's sensible. I work at a primary school, lunchtimes, so I'm sort of on school hours too. I'm a senior midday supervisor, and I do breakfast club. Is it just you with her, then? Sorry, I saw the little polo shirts on the drying rack.
B: Yeah, mostly me. Her mum's in Leicester, she goes some weekends.
A: Same here, sort of. Isla's dad's in Lowestoft, every other weekend. It's alright, we're civil. But the evenings can be a bit quiet, can't they, once they're in bed?
B: Yeah. Yeah, they can. I play FIFA, mostly. Or watch films.
A: I do my Open University stuff, I'm doing a degree part-time. Which is very glamorous, me at the kitchen table at ten o'clock with a highlighter. Do you find the school gate okay? I always think it must be weird for dads, it's all mums chatting.
B: Erm, kind of, yeah. They're friendly. I just sort of stand there. I don't really know what to say about, you know, Pilates.
A: Ha! I'm a mum and I don't know what to say about Pilates either. Honestly, half of them terrify me.
B: Ha, yeah.
A: Do you have to do her hair and everything in the mornings? That was always the battle with Isla.
B: Yeah, I learned plaits off YouTube. Took me ages. Now I can do two in about five minutes.
A: Two plaits in five minutes? That's better than me, I just shove it in a ponytail and hope.
B: Took a lot of practice. She used to cry when I pulled.
A: Bless her. Do you get much help with everything?
B: My mum, she's ten minutes away. She does pick-up if I'm late. And she sends food home with me, way too much. I've got a tub of theplas, I can't finish them.
A: I'd happily take them off your hands. I batch-cook dal and soups because it's cheaper, but nobody sends me anything. Oh, and my mum's got this mardy old Jack Russell, Pickle, who bites everyone except Isla. Do you get out much at the weekend, the two of you?
B: Park, mostly. Behind the flats. I found her a bike on Marketplace for twenty quid, so she's been learning on that.
A: Twenty quid! That's a bargain. Is she getting the hang of it, or is it lots of...
